summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior amputations was admitted for worsening foot wounds on the right heel, lateral foot, and site of prior great toe amputation, with purulent drainage and foul odor. He had been unable to secure an outpatient vascular surgery appointment. Blood pressure was severely elevated on arrival, attributed to missed medications. Imaging showed soft tissue swelling without evidence of osteomyelitis. He was treated with IV antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral Bactrim. Vascular and podiatry teams recommended medical management with betadine dressings and outpatient vascular studies. His hypertension improved with reinitiation of home medications, and transplant function remained stable. He was discharged home with follow-up plans and instructions for wound care and medication adherence.
problems: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
Non-pressure chronic ulcer of right heel and midfoot with unspecified severity
